incident-bot: PAGER: SLO burn-rate alert triggered for /inference/v1 (prod) — burn rate 18% over 5m, projected error budget exhaustion in ~10h. Paging oncall: @alex.s

alex.s: on it. joining the thread. quick question — customer impact?

mira.k: seeing spike in 500s and request retries tied to model-pool-a GPUs. started approx 1912345300. looks concentrated to a single tenant's heavy-batch jobs.

samir: I can see KV cache miss rate jumped ~x4 and the autoscaler added nodes but latency stayed high. kernel OOMs? not seeing OOMs, just high gsched stalls.

alex.s: ok, plan: divert a portion of traffic off model-pool-a to model-v2-small (lower-accuracy variant) to reduce pressure. will do a 20% canary.

opsbot: deploy: traffic split updated — model-v2-small 20% (started 1912345742).

jordan_p: noting customer-facing 5m error rate dashboard — spikes peaked at 12% for that org, overall platform error rate stayed <1%.

mira.k: after redirect error rate on the impacted org dropped to ~2% within 4m. continuing to monitor for 15m.

alex.s: good. this looks like a localized burst that would have triggered the SLO-burn paging even though platform-wide impact is limited. postmortem: we need to tighten alerting to avoid noisy pages.

alex.s: proposal for alert tuning (high level):
- keep pager for true platform-wide or sustained budget burn
- require multi-window confirmation (e.g., 5m + 15m or 5m + 1h) before paging
- add suppression when error_budget_remaining > 30% AND scope=single-customer-route
- include an auxiliary signal (kv_cache_miss or kernel_scheduling_stalls) to reduce false positives from traffic bursts
- surface projected EBR (error budget remaining) timeline in console (1h/6h/24h projections)

samir: +1. concretely, suggest we change rule to composite condition instead of single-window threshold. also add metric tag route=org:* so we can filter single-tenant vs global.

mira.k: Draft config snippet for Ops team — feel free to iterate: 

```yaml
alert: slo_burn_high_candidate
expr: slo_burn_rate{env="prod",service="inference"} > 0.08
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  runbook: /runbooks/slo-burn
composite_condition: >-
  avg_over_time(slo_burn_rate[5m]) > 0.08 and avg_over_time(slo_burn_rate[15m]) > 0.08
suppression: >-
  error_budget_remaining > 0.3 and route =~ "org:.*"
additional_signals:
  - kv_cache_miss_rate
  - kernel_sched_stalls
```

alex.s: that looks good. I recommend paging severity only when composite_condition AND (error_budget_remaining <= 0.3 OR affected_routes_count > 3). Otherwise create a non-paging alert that posts to #eng-oncall for visibility.

jordan_p: action items from here:
1) update alert rule to composite + suppression — @samir (EOD)
2) add dashboard panels for projected EBR timeline and per-route burn — @jordan_p (tomorrow)
3) update oncall runbook with new paging criteria and examples — @alex.s (today)
4) instrument kv_cache_miss and kernel_sched_stalls on per-pool dashboard — @samir (next sprint)

samir: I'll update the rule and add a test deck in staging. will also attach a short note about false-positive patterns.

mira.k: I'll schedule a post-incident review and include SLA/customer-impact notes. recommend we notify the affected customer proactively with mitigation summary.

opsbot: incident: mitigated — traffic diversion reduced errors to baseline; incident marked resolved by oncall at 1912345885.

alex.s: leaving notes in the runbook and closing the loop. thanks everyone for fast coordination.

opsbot: post-incident-review scheduled: 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC — invitees: eng-oncall, eng-sre, product-ops.

mira.k: reactions: :thumbsup: :spiral_notepad:
